fieldComponents.modal: room-mode field including supported boundary loss and room coupling

rules: speaker contributions are summed as complex pressure, not dB magnitudes
gain, delay, polarity, crossover filters, speaker response and directional coupling are applied before summation
disabled SpeakerSets suppress their member contributions without destroying member state
SpeakerSet members are resolved to world transforms and then evaluated as individual Speaker contributions
the modal room field represents low-frequency room response and boundary effects
the direct sound field evaluates propagation from each speaker to each receiver point using distance, phase, world orientation and DirectivityModel
the visualization field crossfades between modal room field and directional direct field instead of summing two total-field approximations and double-counting the direct path
modal Green-function scaling and free-field direct propagation use compatible 1/m field dimensions before hybrid weighting
hybrid transition is explicit and frequency dependent; high-frequency visualization must not require extending the modal eigenbasis to the full UI navigation range
frequency-range visualization must be derived from the same underlying phase-aware field component
the visualization may explicitly select modal, hybrid or direct field components without changing speaker, room or treatment domain state
attached absorptive treatment affects the supported modal boundary-loss model and must not be fabricated as attenuation of the unobstructed direct path
speaker position or orientation changes invalidate affected coupling and field samples immediately
SpeakerSet parent or member transform changes invalidate affected coupling and field samples immediately
interactive visualization recomputes at most once per animation frame and does not wait for drag end
frequencyRange is a requested analysis range and must not imply an unrelated hard-coded global solver maximum
the current hybrid field is an explicitly labelled approximation and must not be described as a full broadband room impulse-response solver
